content.comment_body: Hello, thanks for the helpful discussion. I’m still experiencing issues when setting up a Modbus Client/Server network. I’ve configured the devices and assigned IP addresses, but I’m unable to add a circuit to any device. If I create a new circuit using Network Input or Output blocks, I receive an 'incompatible connector' error when trying to add an input conditioning block. Can anyone advise where I might be going wrong?
Please upload your [product_name] program to the forum.
Here it is. It’s fairly simple—just attempting to set up a Modbus test network with [product_name] as the client and an AB Micro 820 device as the server. Thanks.

In the network view, choose only two MODBUS-compatible devices. However, you must include at least one [product_name] of the correct type. Also, keep in mind that with the IP addresses, it won’t work properly unless the [product_name] uses network class 3, as the IP needs to start with 192.xxx.xxx.xxx.

Thank you for the fast reply. Regarding the [product_name] configuration, I don't see where to define the client/server connection type. How exactly is the communication link established with the second device (Micro820)? Is it solely through the Network Input/Output instruction? I still encounter the 'incompatible connector' error when adding a contact input and connecting it to the input side of the Network Input block. Are there specific block types that can be used for input conditioning?
The video attached demonstrates how to set up the connection between [product_name] (client) and the MODBUS device (server).

I hadn’t considered clicking on the connector—thanks for that tip! The Class 3 (C) network restriction might be an issue for us. Do you know if [company_name] has any plans to support integration with Class A or B networks in future developments?
I’m not aware of any such plans.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter configuration challenges when establishing Modbus TCP communication between [company_name] controllers and other devices. Main issues include selecting compatible devices, network class limitations on IP addressing, and connecting logic in [product_name] programs. Persistent problems involve address restrictions and 'incompatible connector' errors, making it difficult for users trying to integrate equipment from different manufacturers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward integration between [product_name] and other Modbus-capable devices, the ability to configure connections beyond current network and IP limitations, and smooth use of conditioning blocks without compatibility errors.
